description: Hand-written frozen answers for the OTA run-store reducer and the auto-push backoff and wake scheduler. Every value was derived from OtaRunStore.swift, OtaRunStore.kt, OtaService.swift and OtaService.kt read side by side and re-evaluated independently, then checked against both emitted arms - not copied from one of them. That third derivation is what makes the run-store agreement mean something: two arms agreeing could be two arms making the same mistake. An arm conforms when its ota-trace.<impl>.json matches these constants and every step of every case. The rust arm does not exist yet; it arrives with the phase-4 port of the run store and asserts against this file from its first commit. The two companion arms only emit, and stop existing when the shared core replaces them.

reconciled.ret_present: SCOPED TO RUNS. open_run_kind hands back a kind, not a run, and the arms read the contract differently: swift reports ret_present true whenever any optional came back, kotlin only when a run did. Kotlin's reading is frozen, because the contract's own field list says every ret_* run field is null when ret_present is false and swift's answer breaks that invariant - it reports present with all nineteen run fields null. All five divergent steps are open_run_kind calls, ret_open_kind already carries that call's answer, and both arms agree on it. Emitter semantics; no shipped code differs.
reconciled.wake_deadline_ms: INTEGER SECONDS, TRUNCATED TOWARD ZERO. OtaPollConfig.intervalSeconds is a TimeInterval on swift and a Long on kotlin, so a configured 90.5s interval is a 90500ms deadline on one side and 90000ms on the other. No daemon tie-break exists - the poll interval is host-app config and never crosses the wire - so it is decided on merits: the interval is raised to a 60s floor before use, sub-second precision cannot move a poll cadence, and a type that can hold a value the component cannot act on is worth deleting. The shared core carries whole seconds; the swift public surface narrows at its cutover. Only the 90.5 step of the-wake-deadline-floors-the-interval-at-one-minute moves; every whole-second step already agreed.
reconciled.backoff_delay_ms: IDENTICAL, and this is the pair the section exists for. Swift computes min(120s * pow(2, min(n-1, 5)), 900s) in floating-point seconds; kotlin computes min(120000ms shl min(n-1, 5), 900000ms) in integer milliseconds. Side by side they clamp the same exponent before the same ceiling, and pow(2, k) for k <= 5 is exact in a double, so the product is exact across the whole ladder. The twelve-failure sweep confirms it in the uncapped product as well as the capped delay: the raw ladder runs 120000, 240000, 480000, 960000, 1920000, 3840000 and then holds from attempt seven, while the ceiling has held at 900000 since attempt four. The two limiters were separated precisely so neither could hide a disagreement, and neither did. The shared core uses the integer-millisecond form. Closed by the numbers, not by an equivalence argument.
reconciled.run_store: NO DIVERGENCE. Thirty-seven cases, one hundred and forty-three steps, thirty-five fields a step, two independently written arms and one independently derived reference - the reducer agrees everywhere, including the edges neither platform's unit suite covers: a failed PHASE snapshot writes the phase and the error but leaves the outcome unset so the run stays open to dismiss, interrupt and openRunKind; progress after a terminal outcome still rewinds the phase while the outcome stands; and the failed event synthesises a run when nothing was planned. Frozen as conformance for the port.
reconciled.progress_kind_overwrite: OVERRULED BY JOEY 2026-08-05. Both companion arms assigned the progress event's kind unconditionally, so an image progress tick landing on a webapp-install run relabelled the run and the card changed what it claimed to be installing. The corpus could not decide it - two arms agreeing is not a ruling - so the adopted default was to preserve the relabel through the port and revisit it on merits. It was revisited and reversed: a progress tick now only sets the run's kind when the run has none, and the planned kind stands otherwise. The shared reducer drops the tick's kind entirely, because every run in it is opened with a kind by the plan or by the failure that synthesised it, so there is no run without one. The frozen swift and kotlin answer files still carry the old relabel; they record what those implementations did, not what the shared core must do. This case's expectation moved instead: the second step keeps installedWebapp and the open_run_kind call answers installedWebapp.
reconciled.idle_stall_watchdog: OUTSIDE THIS CORPUS, DECIDED ANYWAY. The reducer this corpus drives has no timeout in it; the divergence that mattered sat one level up in OtaService. Swift factors awaitTerminal plus a ProgressClock and fails the run after 60s without progress, while kotlin's inline collectors had no idle branch and suspended forever if the daemon stopped emitting otaProgress mid-apply. Swift wins on the standing rule that the non-hanging side is canonical, and the kotlin fix has landed - OTA_IDLE_DEADLINE_MS is 60000, matching swift. The port carries the watchdog. Recorded here because a clean corpus is not evidence that a component agreed: a trace corpus cannot observe a hang.
reconciled.field_presence: EXPLICIT NULLS. The contract puts every field on every step with inapplicable fields null; swift's JSONEncoder elides nil-valued keys, so its answer file carries up to twenty-nine fewer keys on a step. trace-diff normalises an absent key to null, so nothing was hidden and the reference reproduced swift's answers field for field. This file is written the contract's way, and an arm asserting against it either emits the nulls or treats absent as null.

asymmetries.auto_push: The auto-push cases are not driven through a shipped object on either side - the backoff and wake expressions are private to a service that cannot be constructed without a live gateway, so each arm transcribes its own. Two transcriptions agreeing is weaker evidence than the run store's agreement, which is why this reconcile read both OtaService sources side by side rather than trusting the answer files. The shared core makes these expressions directly testable and this arm becomes behavioural.
